data.narrative:
Radian Aerospace is a seed-stage space and aerospace company that has raised $27.5M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a universe of 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and ICEYE, though direct peer matching at the seed stage remains sparse in this sector.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($27.5M) as a proxy for seed-stage valuation and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier to the next financing round yields an implied post-money valuation of $69M. Public comparables in Space & Aerospace trade at a median P/S multiple of 27.4x across the five tickers, but this method cannot be applied without the target's disclosed revenue, which is not on file. A narrow peer-median approach was not viable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints within the sector.

The single-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $58M (low), $69M (median), and $79M (high), centered on the stage-progression result. The primary uncertainty is the absence of revenue data, which prevents anchoring to public market multiples and would sharpen the range if disclosed. Secondary uncertainty stems from the sparse comparable set at seed stage; the valuation is therefore most sensitive to assumptions about funding round size and dilution in the target's next capital raise.
